claim: The classic renderer decides which wall is in front by products of wall coordinates that overflow 32 bits for very long walls far apart: with sea bands one wall wide, everything past about 38 plan units was drawn under the water in the observer. DWE3M4's longest wall is 71,943; the campaign's longest is 109,061 (E1M7).
evidence: NBlood/source/build/src/engine.cpp:2227 (wallfront: dmulscale2 into int32_t); the same in xmapedit/src/engine.c:876 (wallfront), seen in the XMapEdit observer run of the harbour
projects/blood-city/level/l3_market.py:99-101: the sea's bands; longest walls measured 2026-11-26 with read_map: DWE3M4 71,943, E1M7 109,061 (the campaign's longest)
use: Cut big water and ground sectors so no wall is longer than DWE3M4's longest (about 72k), as Gravesend's sea does.

checked.how: engine.cpp:2227 (wallfront): t1/t2 = dmulscale2(...) of wall coordinate differences into int32_t; xmapedit/src/engine.c:876 the same function. l3_market.py:99-101: the observer run of the harbour, everything past 38 units under the water, DWE3M4's longest 71,943. Measured: DWE3M4 longest wall 71,943; the campaign's longest is 109,061 (E1M7), so 72k is not the campaign's longest.
